name: NHS & respiratory
value: Flu above baseline and rising (wk 45 data)
summary: UKHSA 12 Nov: flu hospital admissions up to 3.65 per 100,000; COVID-19 stable; RSV admissions rising
state: UKHSA's weekly report of 12 Nov, covering 2–8 Nov, says influenza activity has increased and is now above baseline at low levels: lab positivity rose to 8.1% from 7.8% and hospital admissions to 3.65 per 100,000 from 3.00 (UKHSA). COVID-19 is stable at low levels, and RSV hospital admissions rose to 1.30 per 100,000 from 0.89. Flu activity above baseline and rising meets the Watch line; no widespread NHS critical incidents were found as of 15 Nov.
for_you: The NHS advises eligible groups, including over-65s, pregnant women and people with long-term conditions, to get flu and COVID-19 vaccines. UKHSA advises staying home when unwell where possible.
rubric_hit: Watch: flu above baseline and rising (admissions 3.65/100k from 3.00, UKHSA 12 Nov); not high nationally

why: Winter respiratory waves and NHS capacity directly affect access to care for everyone in the UK.
drivers: Flu, COVID, RSV, norovirus, staffing, strikes.

rubric.alert: High or very high flu activity nationally, or widespread critical incidents.
rubric.watch: Respiratory activity above baseline and rising, or several trusts in critical incidents.
rubric.normal: Respiratory activity at baseline and no widespread critical incidents.
